asDecan.p: Every sign is cut into three ten-degree slices called decans, and each slice gets a planet and a small card of its own. Your Sun sits somewhere in the first ten degrees of Taurus, the opening third, where the sign is at its freshest and most like itself. In the old Chaldean order Mercury rules those degrees. Mercury has no special standing in Taurus, it's a visitor there, neither helped nor held back, so it takes on the tone of Venus, who runs the sign. What you get is a quick, counting, talking mind living inside fixed earth, which wants to stay put and keep what it has. The slice after yours is the Six of Pentacles, the Moon's, which is about giving and receiving. After that comes the Seven, Saturn's, waiting on a harvest. Yours is the first one, and it's the one that does the sums. That's why the picture is two people in the snow worrying about what they've got. The Hierophant is still your Sun card, this is just the finer grain inside it.

You know roughly what's in your account without checking, and you check anyway. At the supermarket you notice the price of butter went up forty cents and it stays with you for the afternoon. When friends split a restaurant bill evenly you do the maths on what you actually ate, and then, usually, say nothing. A text left on read from your boss can have you working out what you'd do if the job went, down to which bills you'd cut first, before they've even replied. None of that makes you mean. You're often generous, especially with food and time. But there's a running tally in your head, Mercury keeping the books for a sign that likes to feel safe, and it rarely switches off. A Sunday with nothing planned tends to turn into sorting the budget spreadsheet, and you find that oddly calming.

The less obvious gift is that you notice who's struggling. Because the question of having enough is always somewhere in your thoughts, you pick up on it in other people long before they say anything. A friend who suddenly suggests a picnic instead of dinner out, a colleague who's stopped coming to Friday drinks, a cousin who's gone quiet about the renovation. You clock it, and with Venus colouring the sign you tend to handle it kindly, with no fuss. You're the one who says you over-ordered and can they please take some of this home. You find the cheaper venue for the reunion so the whole group can come, and you never mention why. People who've been through a lean patch often remember you as the person who made it easy for them to accept help.

The shadow isn't really stinginess. It's that you prepare for losses that haven't happened, and the preparing starts to cost more than the loss would. I see this a lot with early Taurus Suns. There's a rumour of restructuring at work and you've spent three weeks quietly miserable, turned down a holiday and snapped at your partner about the power bill, and then the restructure never touches your team. Mercury is quick and Taurus is slow to let go, so a worry arrives fast and then won't leave. The other side of it is pride about asking. You'd rather go without the thing, the loan, the lift to the airport, the favour from your sister, than admit you're short. People close to you sometimes find out months later that you were having a hard time, and that hurts them.

When something goes wrong, a job lost or a diagnosis in the family or a relationship ending, your first move is the numbers. You sit down that night and work out how long the savings last, what gets cancelled, what could be sold. That's useful, and it steadies you. A week later is where it gets harder. The sums are done, but you keep doing them, and you start pulling in. You stop answering the group chat because every plan costs money. You say you're fine. The people around you end up guessing, and they usually guess wrong, which leaves them hovering and you feeling watched. What actually helps is one plain conversation with someone you trust where you say the figure out loud, the real one. Then let them do something practical for you, and don't pay them back straight away.

You show love through provision. A stocked fridge, the good sheets, remembering which brand of tea they like. What people don't always see is how closely you watch whether it's safe to need them. Early in a relationship you're slow to let someone pay, and slower still to let them see your bank balance or your family's troubles. With Venus ruling the sign you're affectionate and physical once you settle, you like being close, but the settling takes a while, and Mercury keeps a quiet count of who gave what. Partners who do best with you tend to be matter-of-fact about money and generous without making a show of it. The trouble spot is when your partner is careless with spending. You won't shout. You'll go cold and start keeping a second, private budget, which is worse.

The Hierophant gives you the respect for how things are done properly. This slice adds a head for the actual figures. You tend to do well anywhere money, stock or supplies have to be tracked and nobody's allowed to lose any of it, bookkeeping, procurement, running a small shop, managing a kitchen, grant writing, a charity's accounts. Mercury makes you a good negotiator on price, patient and polite and quite hard to move. You're also good at explaining money to people who are frightened of it. The usual mistake is underpricing yourself. You'll fight for the company's margin and then accept the first salary offered, because asking for more feels risky. The other one is staying in a secure job years past the point it suited you. Check the market rate for what you do once a year, and ask for it.

At twenty this decan is often anxious about money in a way friends find a bit odd. You're the one with the savings goal and the part-time job, and a fear of being caught short that may or may not match your actual circumstances. Some people with the Sun here grew up with a real shortage, and some just grew up hearing about one. By the mid-thirties the security usually exists on paper, a deposit saved, steady work, and the question becomes whether you'll let yourself feel it. That's commonly when the pride about asking starts to ease, often after a stretch where you had no choice and found people did turn up. The fifties tend to bring a steadier Taurus, still careful, but spending on what you enjoy without the running commentary, and quick to help younger people through their own lean years.

Keep a small amount of money each month that's set aside for spending on nothing useful. It doesn't go to savings or bills or presents for other people. Thirty dollars, fifty, whatever's comfortable. Spend all of it by the end of the month on something you enjoy, flowers, a good lunch alone, a book you'll probably never finish. Don't carry it over. When the worrying voice starts totting up what else it could have gone on, let it finish, and buy the thing anyway.
